papers_read.title_as_printed: Multi-scale enhanced graph convolutional network for mild cognitive impairment detection (Lei et al.; Pattern Recognition 2023)
Regularized spatio-temporal weighted graph convolution network based on multimodal fusion for mild cognitive impairment detection (Wu, Dong, Wu; Expert Syst Appl 2026)

what_each_reports.P-14: 184 ADNI subjects (77 EMCI, 40 LMCI, 67 NC), rs-fMRI + DTI connectivity (LWCC features), population-graph MSE-GCN, leave-one-out: EMCI vs NC 85.42%, LMCI vs NC 93.46%, LMCI vs EMCI 92.31%, three-class 83.11% (Table 3). The abstract's 'mean classification accuracy of 90.39%' equals the mean of the three binary tasks.
what_each_reports.P-79: ADNI2 (161 NC, 147 EMCI, 128 LMCI) and ADNI3 (244 NC, 190 MCI), rs-fMRI + T1 gray-matter volume + age/sex population graph (MCRSW-GCN), stratified 5-fold CV: NC vs LMCI 97.44%, EMCI vs LMCI 95.56%, NC vs EMCI 95.39%, three-class 92.55%, ADNI3 NC vs MCI 87.08% (Tables 3-7). The '+8.5%' in the abstract is 'an average improvement of 8.5% in accuracy over baseline models', a relative claim about its own comparison, not an accuracy.

quantity_a: Mean of three ADNI binary accuracies (EMCI/NC, LMCI/NC, LMCI/EMCI) from rs-fMRI+DTI connectivity features, LOOCV.
quantity_b: As recorded: an average accuracy improvement of P-79's model over its own re-run baselines (a difference in percentage points), not an accuracy of any classifier.
incompatible_if_same: No. The record's gap of 0.819 is 0.9039 minus 0.085, i.e. an accuracy set against an improvement margin, which is arithmetic on unlike quantities. On the per-task accuracies both papers actually report (for example NC vs LMCI 93.46% vs 97.44%; NC vs EMCI 85.42% vs 95.39%), the two are different methods on different modality pairs (DTI vs T1) and different ADNI subsets with different validation (LOOCV vs 5-fold), and neither paper claims an ordering that the other refutes.

gates.task: match: both CN/EMCI/LMCI discrimination within the MCI spectrum (T1).
gates.dataset_family: match: ADNI for both (different subsets and phases; overlapping subjects possible but not stated).
gates.validation_tier: match in tier (internal CV only): LOOCV vs stratified 5-fold.
gates.modality_family: partial: both rs-fMRI, but P-14 adds DTI structural connectivity and P-79 adds T1 gray-matter volume and a phenotype graph.

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible as recorded (accuracy vs relative improvement); compatible metric type only if P-79's per-task accuracies are substituted, which the record did not do.
performance_validity: Not a valid performance comparison as recorded. If P-79's per-task accuracies were used, its NC vs LMCI 97.44% (AUC 99.75%) is at or above 0.97 on internal 5-fold CV with no external MCI cohort (its only external test is an MDD dataset), so the exclusion would apply to that task.
independence: Distinct author groups. Both use ADNI; P-79 does not state its subject IDs, so overlap with P-14's 184 subjects cannot be excluded.
grounds: The record's claim_b misreads P-79: '+8.5% vs baseline' is an average improvement over the paper's own baselines, not a classification accuracy, so there is no second result on the contested quantity.
P-14's 90.39% is itself a composite, the mean of three different binary tasks, not a single estimand.

On the task-matched accuracies both papers do report, the results are two different methods' scores on different modality pairs with no refuted ordering, and P-79's NC vs LMCI figure would fall under the performance-validity exclusion.

MCRSW-GCN, achieves ACC values of 97.44%, 95.56%, 95.39%, 87.08%, and 92.55% in the five tasks (NC vs. LMCI, EMCI vs. LMCI, NC vs. EMCI, NC vs. MCI, and the three-class classification
We adopted stratified five-fold cross-validation to evaluate model performance.
our method is promising to detect MCI and superior to other competing algorithms, with a mean classification accuracy of 90.39% in the detection tasks.
In the four classification tasks, our proposed method has the best mean accuracy of 85.42%, 93.46%, and 92.31%, 83.11% respectively.

record_defects: claim_b 'P-79: +8.5% vs baseline' treats a relative improvement as a performance result; gap_magnitude 0.819 is computed from unlike quantities.
claim_a '90.39%' is P-14's mean over three binary tasks, not the result of any single task.
modality_family 'functional_mri' omits that P-14 fuses DTI and P-79 fuses T1 structural MRI.
The pack registry lists P-79 Best_Metric as 'not reported' although the paper reports per-task accuracies (97.44%, 95.56%, 95.39%, 87.08%, 92.55%).
what_would_change_the_verdict: Nothing about the record as written. A new candidate built on task-matched accuracies would still need the same modality pair and a refuted ordering, and P-79's 97.44% NC vs LMCI would first need an external cohort to escape the performance-validity exclusion.
